title: Instructions
text:
I created this website to prep for office hours, mainly to practice setting it up in Positron.

Open a Positron folder in the general folder where you’d like to set up your website. For example: Desktop, Documents, Downloads, etc.
Open the terminal (shortcut: Control + backtick (`)).

Type and enter: quarto create project website
Enter your desired website name: first-last.github.io
Enter the title: First Last

Publish the folder to a public GitHub repository via Positron. Commit, pull, and push as you make changes to your website.
You now have a couple of new files. index.qmd is the homepage, about.qmd is the About page, and _quarto.yml is essentially the blueprint for the website. You can also edit index.qmd and about.qmd to your liking. You can also create new .qmd files for additional pages and add them to _quarto.yml.
Add any desired documents (resume, photos, posters, presentation slides, etc.) to this new folder. These documents can be placed in a subfolder named files.
Click the Preview button to see what your website looks like.
When you’re ready to publish your website, follow the steps in this helpful link to publish your website to GitHub Pages. Essentially, do the following:

Add output-dir: docs to the _quarto.yml file under type: website.
Now work in the terminal:

Add a .nojekyll file to the root of your repository:

Mac/Linux: touch .nojekyll
Windows: copy NUL .nojekyll

Run the following in the terminal:
quarto render
git add docs
git commit -m "Publish site to docs/"
git push

Finally, configure your GitHub repository to publish from the docs directory of your main branch. On github.com, go to the Settings tab of your GitHub repository, then Pages. Select main as the branch and /docs as the folder. Click Save.

Refresh and view your deployed website. It may take a few minutes for the website or new changes to appear.
KEY: Every time you make a change to your website, you must hit the Preview button and then commit and push those changes so that the HTML is updated. The changes will not be reflected on your website until you do this. It may take a few minutes for the changes to appear. Just refresh.
